annotationRationale: Similarity locates the altitude foot, and equal-height area comparisons determine the division ratio. The verified equivalent shared-bank problem supplies two reviewed, genuinely distinct methods. Coordinate line equations and distances remain specific to the alternative route.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independently, with shortest leg 1, similarity gives hypotenuse projections \(BH=1/2\) and \(AH=3/2\). Equal-area comparison gives \(HP:CP=3:4\), so the smaller fraction is \(3/7\), choice A. The supplied source figure uses B as the right-angle vertex; the candidates consistently relabel it C. This creates no contradiction. The additional source-figure construction is unnecessary to either explanation.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: For the identical 2025_AMC_10B_Q13, similarity-and-equal-areas and coordinate-intersections are independently verified and retained with their exact method credits. The historical similarity-and-areas and coordinate-intersection entries contain no worked explanations and are merged into their corresponding retained routes. LIVE's coordinate route and Random Math's area route are represented. Random Math's mass-points route is omitted reasonably because it expresses the same balancing relationship while requiring an additional technique; the retained synthetic and coordinate methods already offer useful distinct approaches.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed similarity, area, and proportional-segment concepts match the main route. The 30-degree triangle property, median, and altitude are appropriate support. The alternative's slope, line-equation, intersection, and distance concepts are correctly method-specific. Equal-height area ratios are explicitly derived and need no additional catalog node.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: AA similarity gives \(BH/BC=BC/BA\), hence \(AH/AB=3/4\). Both median-area equalities and the subtraction yielding equal areas of ABP and ACP are correct. The two common-height comparisons then give \(HP/CP=3/4\), correctly identifying HP as shorter and producing \(3/7\).
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The reused method exactly matches 2025_AMC_10B_Q13#similarity-and-equal-areas. Its shared-reference ID and inherited randommath-reference-2025_AMC_10B_Q13 ID are both retained. The supplied method-local provenance supports project reuse, and no official MAA authorship is claimed.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The point definitions suffice without another diagram. Similarity correspondence, equal-area subtraction, and both area-to-base ratios are explained. The final smaller-segment identification is explicit.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_271 and cnm_272 cover similarity and corresponding-side ratios; cnm_p148 supplies the common-height area comparisons; cnm_268 covers conversion of the segment ratio to a part-of-whole fraction.
